covers.quote: Italicise genus and species names
Genus and species names are in italics.

examples.note: Backhousia has an initial capital and is in italics

parts.quote: Backhousia citriodora is the scientific name of the lemon myrtle.

examples.note: Ornithorhynchus has an initial capital and is in italics

parts.quote: Ornithorhynchus anatinus is the scientific name of the platypus.

rules.quote: the genus is in italics and takes an initial capital
rules.violation_condition: a genus name written without italics or without an initial capital letter
when: In scientific classification names of plants and animals
rules.why: G-1 and G-4: The heading covers both genus and species, but genus and species have distinct capitalisation rules, so each list item defines the actionable rule.

covers.quote: Species names are in lower case.

examples.note: citriodora is lowercase and italicised

parts.quote: Backhousia citriodora is the scientific name of the lemon myrtle.

examples.note: anatinus is lowercase and italicised

parts.quote: Ornithorhynchus anatinus is the scientific name of the platypus.

rules.quote: the species is in italics and is lower case.
rules.violation_condition: a species epithet/name written without italics or with an initial capital letter
when: In scientific classification names of plants and animals
rules.why: G-1 and G-4: Formulates the specific requirement for species names.

covers.quote: The abbreviations are in roman type and lower case. The subspecies and varietal names themselves are in italics.
For animals, there is only one taxonomic level below that of species: subspecies. By convention, the abbreviation ‘subsp.’ is not used.

examples.note: 'subsp.' is in roman type with a full stop, while 'hedraia' is italicised

parts.quote: Eucalyptus pauciflora subsp. hedraia is a subspecies of snow gum found only in the Mount Bogong and Falls Creek areas of Victoria.

examples.note: 'var.' is in roman type with a full stop, while 'platyptera' is italicised

parts.quote: Acacia alata var. platyptera is a variety of winged wattle that is found only in Western Australia.

rules.quote: Subspecies and the names of varieties are also italicised. In these names, abbreviations for the words ‘subspecies’ and ‘variety’ take a full stop.
rules.violation_condition: subspecies or variety names written in roman type, or abbreviations for subspecies and variety written without a full stop or in italics
when: Writing botanical or zoological subspecies and varieties
For animals, the abbreviation 'subsp.' is not used
rules.why: G-2: Consolidates the formatting of botanical/zoological subcategories and their abbreviations.

rules.quote: Use the semantic tag <em> to provide emphasis for italicised names in HTML.
rules.violation_condition: italicised plant or animal scientific names coded in HTML using styling or tags other than the semantic <em> tag
when: Content authored in HTML
rules.why: Specific accessibility instruction for web markup.

covers.quote: Use lower case unless they are also a proper noun, a registered trade mark or in some specialised content such as genetics.
Do not use italics.
Use initial capitals when the name includes a proper noun.
Names that have become everyday words are shown in roman type and don’t need a capital letter.
You usually don’t need to use an initial capital for breeds, even if they are derived from a regional name.
In generalist Australian Government content, use lower case for the names of birds unless the name contains a proper noun.
In both generalist and specialist content, use lower case for bird names in a list of common names of plants and animals.

examples.note: Tasmanian devil retains capital only on proper noun 'Tasmanian'

parts.quote: The Tasmanian devil is named after its home range of Tasmania.

examples.note: red kangaroos in lowercase and roman type

parts.quote: The grasslands were home to more than a million red kangaroos.

examples.note: Capitalised only for the proper noun 'Norfolk Island'

parts.quote: Norfolk Island pine

examples.note: silver gull in lowercase

parts.quote: The silver gull (Larus novaehollandiae) is a common gull of the Australian coast.

examples.note: All common names in lowercase in a list

parts.quote: The area was inhabited by green tree frogs, carpet pythons, bush rats and silver gulls.

rules.quote: Write common names in lower case and roman type
rules.violation_condition: a common name of a plant or animal written in italics or with an initial capital letter when it is not a proper noun, registered trade mark, or specialised ornithological/genetic context
when: Unless they include a proper noun (e.g. Tasmanian devil, Norfolk Island pine)
Unless it is a registered trade mark or cultivar name
Unless in specialised context such as international ornithology conventions or genetics
In a list of common names of plants and animals, use lower case even for bird names
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: The heading concisely states the rule; child bullet points, breeds, everyday names, and bird name rules are specific sub-cases or restatements folded into when.

examples.note: Cascade is initial capitalised and in single quotation marks

parts.quote: Acacia ‘Cascade’ is a registered cultivar derived from Australian native flora.

rules.quote: Use an initial capital for names of registered cultivars or breeds.
rules.violation_condition: a registered cultivar or breed name written without an initial capital letter
when: In a sentence, the registered name is sometimes in quotation marks
rules.why: G-2: Standalone rule for registered trade marks / cultivar names.

examples.note: Gene Sbe1 is in italics

parts.quote: In plants, the gene Sbe1 encodes starch-branching enzyme one, Sbe1.

rules.quote: Use italics for the names of genes.
rules.violation_condition: the name of a gene written in roman type instead of italics
when: When using genetic terms for plants and animals
rules.why: Distinct typographic rule for gene names.

covers.quote: Capitalisation varies for the names of genes, but proteins usually take an initial capital only.

examples.note: Protein Sbe1 is in roman type

parts.quote: In plants, the gene Sbe1 encodes starch-branching enzyme one, Sbe1.

rules.quote: Use roman type for the names of proteins (enzymes).
rules.violation_condition: the name of a protein or enzyme written in italics instead of roman type
when: When using genetic terms for plants and animals
Proteins usually take an initial capital only
rules.why: Distinct typographic rule for protein names.

covers.quote: Include the genus and species at first mention of the common name

examples.note: Scientific name Grevillea victoriae follows Royal grevillea in parentheses

parts.quote: Royal grevillea (Grevillea victoriae) is one of more than 350 species in the genus Grevillea.

rules.quote: include the species name in parentheses when you first mention the common name so it is clear which plant or animal you are writing about.
rules.violation_condition: the common name of a plant or animal is first mentioned in a text without its scientific/species name in parentheses
when: At first mention of the common name of a plant or animal
rules.why: G-4: Heading restated in body sentence.

covers.quote: When the genus is repeated, it can be abbreviated
When there are several genera that start with the same letter, include the second letter in the abbreviation.

examples.note: Abbreviated to O. anatinus on second mention

parts.quote: Ornithorhynchus anatinus belongs to the Ornithorhynchidae family. The elusive O. anatinus can be spotted in the riparian zone of our freshwater rivers.

examples.note: Abbreviated to An. and Al. to distinguish genera

parts.quote: Anopterus macleayanus and Aleuries moluccana are small Australian trees. Although An. macleayanua is found in cool places, Al. moluccana can tolerate tropical conditions.

rules.quote: If you have already written the full name of the genus, use a shortened form for later mentions.
rules.violation_condition: a genus name written out in full on subsequent mentions after its first full mention, rather than abbreviated to its initial letter (or first two letters if multiple genera share the same initial)
when: The full genus name has already been written earlier in the document
Shortened form is often the first letter followed by a full stop (e.g. O. anatinus)
When several genera share the same initial letter, include the second letter (e.g. An. macleayanus, Al. moluccana)
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: Heading is candidate; body sentence states actionable instruction and incorporates disambiguation condition.

covers.quote: Names down to genus level start with capital letters.

examples.note: Myrtaceae is roman type with initial capital

parts.quote: Backhousia citriodora is in the family Myrtaceae.

examples.note: Monotremata is roman type with initial capital

parts.quote: Ornithorhynchus anatinus is in the order Monotremata.

rules.quote: All classification names above genus level are in roman type and take initial capitals.
rules.violation_condition: a taxonomic classification name above genus level (kingdom, phylum, class, order, family) written in italics or with a lowercase initial letter
when: Taxonomic ranks above genus (e.g. family, order, class, phylum, kingdom)
rules.why: Clear structural formatting rule for taxonomic ranks above genus.

covers.quote: Scientific names can include the name of a person

Plants and animals are sometimes allocated to a different genus from the one they were given when they were first described. In this case, the name and date appear in parentheses after the genus and species name.

examples.note: F.Muell. is in roman type

parts.quote: Grevillea victoriae F.Muell. was first described by botanist Ferdinand von Mueller.

examples.note: (Walker, 1869) is in roman type inside parentheses

parts.quote: Robshelfordia circumducta (Walker, 1869)

rules.quote: The name and date, if they are included, appear in roman type.
rules.violation_condition: the author name or publishing date following a scientific species name written in italics rather than roman type
when: In technical content that includes the authority (person who first described the species) and publication date
If the species has been reallocated to a different genus, the name and date appear in parentheses after the species name
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: Candidate heading folded into typographic rule for authority citation.
